summary: A 1936 wooden lookout on Grass Mountain near Enumclaw, cut down in 1958 and felled in 1980; the footings now serve as a parking area on private timber land.

facts.design: Wooden tower with cabin; a DNR live-in cab was added on top in 1958
facts.status_note: Felled in 1980. A 2016 WillhiteWeb visit found the tower footings used for parking; communication towers stand on the ridge's highest point.

access.note: As of 2016 the timber company charged for access, with non-motorized daily permits ($8 individual, $15 family). Check current rules; the Muckleshoot tribe bought the White River Tree Farm around 2013.

visit.trail_note: Take Highway 410 east out of Enumclaw to a gated pullout, then about 8 miles of logging roads (2016 WillhiteWeb route).

events.note: 100-foot wooden tower and cabin. WillhiteWeb dates the tower to 1937 and gives 105 feet.
Army Aircraft Warning Service use began March 7, 1942; the AWS added a portable 14 by 32 cabin.
AWS use ended October 16, 1943; the State kept the site for fire detection.
Tower cut down with a DNR live-in cab added. Height is 50 ft in the register and firelookout.com; 70 ft in WillhiteWeb.
Ground house sold and torn down to make way for an FAA tower.
DNR Lands Division suggested the site be used as a communications tower lease.
Sue Gunn was the last full-time lookout.
Tower felled into the canyon toward Lynn Lake, the last one in the district. The register's 1979 date conflicts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, firelookout.com and the Rex's page give 1936 and 100 feet; WillhiteWeb gives 1937 and 105 feet. The story uses 1936 and 100 feet as the majority figures and notes WillhiteWeb's version.
The register and firelookout.com say 50 feet; WillhiteWeb says 70 feet. The story reports both figures without choosing one.
The register says gone by 1979. firelookout.com says gone 1980, and WillhiteWeb's first-hand account says the tower was felled in 1980. The story uses 1980.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: agency, gone status and 2012 registration match the sources; nothing to correct. The brief's height_m 30.5 is the original 100 ft; the sources say the tower was cut to 50 or 70 ft in 1958, so the current height is not recorded in the facts. Access is marked permission from 2016 sources only; check current rules before publishing. The WillhiteWeb page has photos that are not recorded here because no image URLs were confirmed.
